item.title: Polyphon Audio: Local Voice Playground
item.description: A local-first playground for voice cloning, voice design, multi-voice narration, sound generation, and live conversational voice. Built on audio.cpp, Polyphon Audio runs entirely on your own hardware, with a resident inference server, Gradio Studio, and integration with Polyphon AI for fully local audio-to-spoken-reply workflows.

item.title: Revamping Autonomous HDB Agents
item.description: A technical walkthrough of revamping Autonomous HDB DeepAgents: replacing PostgreSQL/PostGIS with in-memory SQLite and native Python geodetics, integrating XGBoost valuations into LangGraph, and adding temporal comparability checks to avoid misleading price comparisons. Python now renders the numerical tables deterministically, while the LLM interprets the results. The post also covers data refresh, OneMap geocoding verification, reproducible benchmarks, and the design trade-offs behind constrained autonomy.

item.title: Polyphon AI: Local Meeting Intelligence
item.description: Polyphon AI is an open-source, local-first meeting intelligence engine that captures dual-stream audio, performs real-time and offline speaker diarization, and maintains persistent speaker identities through VoiceDB. It combines low-latency streaming feedback with higher-context post-call reconciliation, then generates self-contained interactive HTML meeting artifacts. Designed for local or private infrastructure, Polyphon AI explores how meeting transcripts can evolve from disposable summaries into a persistent, user-controlled knowledge layer.

item.title: From Photos to Printable 3D
item.description: Building a local AI pipeline that turns photos into watertight, slicer-ready STLs on AMD hardware.

item.title: From Brackets to Enclosures
item.description: A Raspberry Pi 5 snap-fit enclosure puts blender-mcp-bridge through a more demanding agentic test. Claude and Codex successfully construct and verify base-and-lid geometry, while Google Antigravity takes a different path and generates Blender Python instead. The experiment highlights an important distinction: MCP provides the modeling capabilities, but each agent decides how to use them.

item.title: Blender MCP for n8n
item.description: Blender MCP for n8n is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) bridge that allows n8n AI workflows to directly control Blender’s Python API. The system combines a Blender addon, a stateless/stateful MCP bridge server, and a record-and-replay session framework to enable deterministic, reproducible 3D scene generation from natural language. With 70+ structured tools spanning modeling, materials, animation, architectural workflows, and MEP systems, complex scenes can be constructed, tested, and replayed reliably through AI-directed tool calls.

item.title: Engineering a Narrative Multiverse
item.description: Living Storybook explores what happens when storytelling is treated as a system rather than a stream of text. This post walks through the architecture behind a multiverse-aware writing tool that supports branching narratives, causal persistence, and human–AI co-authoring. From timeline reconstruction and chapter blueprints to validation guards and stateful characters, it shows how narrative, planning, and control flow come together to make stories that can truly diverge — without losing coherence.
